scope.mobileContexts: Fresh iPhone 13 settings with explicit 390×844 and 844×390 viewports, isMobile=true, hasTouch=true, reduced motion. Native WebKit with mobile emulation, not physical iOS/Safari device QA.
scope.fixturePolicy: Normal production lobby and fresh duel; no source imports, injected game fixtures, engine-state writes or extra simulation workers.

methods.touch: Tap supplied battlefield/select inspect, start duel, Browse hand, mulligan Replace/Keep, CardDetail Details, Keep hand, Check availability, Select card, Duel menu and log/rules/saves links.
methods.forms: selectOption exercises champion deck and starting-player HTML selects; check selects Beginner difficulty.
methods.keyboard: First/last control focus followed by native Tab/Shift+Tab verifies wrapping. Enter toggles AI summary; Escape closes top nested CardDetail, hand, menu and handoff dialogs and verifies focus restoration. PageDown at focused dialog and modal end verifies stable background position.
methods.interactionReadiness: Wait for phase=main, priorityPlayer=0, turnStep=main, review=null and paused!=true before interactive hand checks.
methods.mobileScrollLimitation: Playwright mouse.wheel is unsupported in isMobile WebKit; touchscreen API has no swipe. Mobile lock evidence covers overflow/reference counting and PageDown, not physical iOS touch scrolling.
methods.wheelCompanion: Separate fresh WebKit contexts at the same sizes use isMobile=false and hasTouch=true for native wheel support. Wheel on backdrop and after modal body reaches its end checks background position through close; mobile touch scrolling remains unverified.

nativePreparation.initialLimitation: Default WebKit launch blocked by seven missing host libraries.
nativePreparation.resolution: Downloaded browser cache via Playwright CLI. Fetched signed official Debian trixie indexes into scratch; apt-get download retrieved .deb libraries and dpkg-deb -x extracted them locally. Scratch launcher sets task-only LD_LIBRARY_PATH and bundled WebKit paths.

limits: No physical iOS device, Safari application or touch-swipe verification.
No full-match simulation or combat/Hidden/crowded-board engine regression in this WebKit follow-up; those have separate Chromium/engine evidence.
Page-error and horizontal-overflow assertions cover the two mobile flows. Separate wheel companion measures scroll position and lock restoration only.
